metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is below recent low, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >45), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model may overreact — cap forecast increase at +3–5% above prior peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- When true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often lags — add 1–2 days of downward adjustment in forecast horizon.  
- If history shows high volatility (e.g., 3+ consecutive large swings), model tends to over-smooth — increase forecast variance or add ±2–3% buffer around median.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
